title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page examines the relationship between film budgets and worldwide revenues. Figure 1 shows budget against revenue for the films in the dataset.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (millions of US dollars)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film budgets and worldwide revenues

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
This page examines the relationship between film runtime and IMDb rating. Figure 1 shows how ratings vary across films with different runtimes.
plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime and IMDb rating

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

This page examines the James Bond films in the dataset.

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()








The Bond films in this dataset run from 1995 to 2021.
